name: C1. Gemach licensing, periodic-report and AML-policy workspace
buyer: Gemach institutions (interest-free deposit and credit funds, mostly charedi and community-run) that need a Capital Market Authority licence; size tiers: under NIS 1m exempt, NIS 1-8m basic licence, over 8m extended
trigger: Gemach Law (supervision of interest-free deposit and credit services, in force 2022): licence application, then periodic automated reports to the Authority (cash flow, donations, deposits, active credit, loans in arrears, loan-to-deposit ratio, liquidity), written AML/CFT risk policy reviewed yearly, a dedicated AML officer, industry-specific AML order
evidence: funder.co.il/article/209090 (3 Sept 2026: first 7 licences issued; Authority exercising enforcement and sending hearing letters); ice.co.il/finance/news/article/1093943 (170+ applications pending, only about 20 mature, no interim licence); tradersunion.com Hebrew item on automated reporting and AML officer; funder.co.il/article/189209 (size tiers, 3-year application window). Funder and Traders Union pages blocked on direct fetch (403); details come from search snippets
existing: Competitor search 'תוכנה לניהול גמ"ח': no Israeli gemach-specific software found; only generic loan software and a community-lending app (CrediGestor/Do Easy). Many gemachim keep Excel. Not checked: whether the Authority provides its own reporting portal, or whether bank-integration or charedi accounting vendors already serve gemachim
unchecked: Final reporting circular and format; Authority portal; number of licensed vs applying gemachim; accountants and charedi-sector vendors; willingness to pay; payment path (donation-funded bodies)

first_check.duty: Licensing under the Gemach Law (in force 2022). Sector AML order (Prohibition on Money Laundering order for interest-free deposit and credit gemachim, התשפ"ו-2026). Capital Market Authority draft circular (2 Aug 2026; comments due end of August; takes effect 18 months after final publication): written AML/CFT risk policy discussed by the board or management committee, an AML officer, and a yearly report due 31 March in a fixed-template file submitted online, plus separate periodic financial reports (draft circular from Oct 2025: cash flow, donations, deposits, credit, loans in arrears; actuarial opinion for complex gemachim). Penalties not verified. Licensing in practice has been slow: news reports said about 20 of 170+ applications were mature, and the claim says the first 7 licences were issued in Sept 2026 (not independently fetched).
first_check.market: More than 170 licence applications pending (Knesset committee figures cited by ICE). Gemachim under NIS 1m are exempt. I found no register count of all financial gemachim. The serviceable market is probably a few hundred bodies at most.
first_check.competitor: No gemach-specific compliance or reporting software found in Hebrew or English searches. Generic loan-servicing software exists. Nedarim Plus (charedi payments platform) terminals are used to log in to at least one large gemach's member portal (JDN). That makes it a likely competitor or channel; whether it offers a gemach management module was not verified. The Authority's own online upload system handles submission only, not data preparation. Charedi accountants and accounting vendors were not checked (not_reached).
first_check.reason: The duty is real, but parts are not yet in force. The licensing duty is law (in force 2022, per ICE). The sector AML order for gemachim is dated 2026 (התשפ"ו-2026). The Capital Market Authority's risk-management circular was still a draft on 2 Aug 2026 (Calcalist). It takes effect 18 months after final publication and requires a written policy approved by the board, a responsible AML officer, and a yearly report due 31 March in a fixed template uploaded to an online system that rejects files not matching it. In three Hebrew and one English search, plus a check of Nedarim Plus, I found no gemach-specific compliance software. The market is small: about 170 licence applicants. Many are informal, donation-funded charedi bodies that are hard to reach and may not pay much. Nedarim Plus already powers some gemach member portals, so it could become a rival.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The main weaknesses are a small market (about 170 applicants, about 20 near-ready) and slow phase-in (AML circular in full effect 1.5 years after final publication; 2 years after first licence to prepare).
challenge_check.reason: I found no product, free state tool or rule that kills this. Hebrew and English searches turned up no gemach-specific management or reporting software, only generic loan systems such as CAV Systems and Nortridge, and the CrediGestor extension. The Authority's online system only accepts and validates files in a fixed template; it does not prepare the data. Two things push the score down. The market is very small: about 170 licence applications are pending and only about 20 are near-ready (ice.co.il). Deadlines are also slow: the AML circular takes full effect 1.5 years after final publication, and licensees get 2 years after licensing (Calcalist). On top of that, donation-funded bodies have limited willingness to pay, and charedi accountants or Nedarim Plus could act as competitors or channels. I didn't check either of them.
